verdict.rationale: Babylon.js is a code-first JavaScript engine, so its core features are exposed as programmatic APIs with TypeScript typings: the full scene graph, mesh and CSG manipulation, physics, and GUI elements. Its visual tools (Inspector scene editing, Node Material Editor, Sandbox) appear only as UI features, and nothing in the pack says their operations can also be done in code, so parity with the UI is implied rather than shown. Missing for 10: an explicit statement of API/UI parity, evidence that Node Material Editor and Inspector edits are reproducible via API, and independent hands-on confirmation of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Provides a complete scene graph with lights, cameras, materials, meshes, sprites, layers, animations, audio clips, GUI elements, and actions
Meshes & Geometry: Primitive shapes, CSG operations, mesh manipulation
